title: The last days
hookLine: in his final illness he leaves no slave behind, gives away his last coins, and asks for the prayer to be kept

cards: A small room beside the mosque in Medina. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is ill with a fever, and it isn't lifting. People come and go quietly.
Aisha, his wife, is caring for him. And in these days, with little strength, the reports remember him busy with two things: giving things away, and one instruction he keeps coming back to.
What does a person hold on to, at the very end, and what do they let go of? Today: the last days.

teach.b: Start with the coins. In a report in the Musnad of Ahmad, Aisha tells that during his illness he had a few gold coins at home, and he asked her to give them away.
Then, in his fever, he asked again: what happened to the coins? She hadn't managed it yet, busy caring for him.
He had them brought, and gave them away, and asked how it would be for him to meet his Lord with these still in his house. Then what he left.
Sahih al-Bukhari records that when he died he left behind no dinar, no dirham, no slave, man or woman, nothing except his white mule, his weapons, and a piece of land he had given as charity.
Whatever he had, he'd already let go of. And then what he held on to.
Sunan Abu Dawud records his last instruction: the prayer, the prayer, and be mindful of God regarding those your right hands possess, the enslaved people and servants of a household.
Of everything he could have said, he repeated that. Keep the prayer.
Look after the people who are under your power. Coins given away the moment he remembered them. A house with nothing left to leave.
And a last word that points away from things, toward the prayer and toward the people with the least power. Ali, who reports it, says these were his last words; Aisha remembers others.
Tomorrow stays in that small room a little longer.

how: Muslims retell the Prophet's final illness from the hadith collections, and his last instruction about the prayer and those in one's care is quoted in teaching about salah.

games.why: he had them brought and gave them away, asking how he could meet his Lord with them still in the house.

practice: Picture a drawer, a shelf or a wallet, and find one thing you're keeping only because you haven't decided; choose it, and decide who it will go to.

Then rest on the other half of his last words, the prayer and the people in your care: if you pray, let this be a moment to remember your next prayer; if not, bring to mind one person who depends on you.

wordCard.voice: The last days. In his final illness the Prophet gave away his last coins, left nothing behind, and asked, again and again, for the prayer to be kept. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the prayer, the word in his last instruction, repeated.

carryVoice: Your line: keep the prayer. Let go of the things; hold on to the prayer and the people. Until tomorrow.
